### ## What's This? PHP syntax is the set of rules that govern how PHP code is written and interpreted by the engine. It is the grammar of the language -- you must arrange words, symbols, and punctuation in the correct order for the computer to understand your instructions. PHP is a server-side scripting language designed for web development, meaning it runs on the server before sending HTML to the browser. It exists because building dynamic websites requires generating content programmatically rather than editing static HTML files by hand. PHP's syntax borrows from C, Perl, and Java, making it familiar to developers from those backgrounds. ### ## The Big Picture PHP powers roughly three-quarters of websites using a server-side language, including platforms like WordPress and Wikipedia. Its syntax integrates with HTML through tags, making it natural for templating. Understanding variables, data types, operators, strings, and arrays is the foundation for everything from vanilla scripts to frameworks like Laravel and Symfony. PHP is forgiving via loose typing but offers strict typing when you opt in. ### ## Core Ideas ### Variables and Data Types Variables start with $ and need no explicit type declaration -- PHP infers the type from the assigned value. The eight primitive types are boolean, integer, float, string, array, object, resource, and null. ```php $name = "Alice"; // string - a sequence of characters $age = 30; // integer - a whole number without decimals $height = 5.8; // float - a decimal number $isAdmin = true; // boolean - true or false value $colors = ["red", "blue"]; // array - ordered collection of items ``` ### Strings and Concatenation PHP has single and double-quoted strings. Double quotes interpret variables and escape sequences; single quotes treat everything literally. The dot operator . concatenates strings. ```php $greeting = "Hello, $name!"; // double quotes interpolate $name to "Alice" $literal = 'Hello, $name!'; // single quotes output $name literally $combined = "Hello " . "World"; // dot operator joins two strings together $now = "Time: " . date('H:i'); // dot chains a function result with a string ``` ### Arrays Arrays are ordered maps supporting integer and string keys. They hold mixed types and grow dynamically. ```php $fruits = ["apple", "banana"]; // indexed array uses default integer keys $user = ["name" => "Alice", "age" => 30]; // associative array uses named keys echo $fruits[0]; // outputs "apple" via integer index access echo $user["name"]; // outputs "Alice" via string key access $fruits[] = "cherry"; // appends "cherry" at the next integer index ``` ### Operators Arithmetic, comparison, logical, and assignment operators manipulate values. The difference between == (loose) and === (strict) is critical because PHP type-jugs automatically. ```php $sum = 10 + 5; // addition operator returns 15 $isEqual = (5 == "5"); // loose equality: true because values match $isIdentical = (5 === "5"); // strict equality: false because types differ $isAdult = ($age >= 18 && $age <= 120); // logical AND combines two comparisons ``` ### ## Wiring It Together This script processes a registration form, validates input, and returns a response: ```php 0) { // if any errors were collected echo "

Errors:

"; // render error section heading foreach ($errors as $error) { // iterate every error in the array echo "

$error

"; // display each error in a paragraph tag } } else { $welcome = "Welcome, $name!"; // interpolate name into greeting string $domain = substr(strstr($email, "@"), 1); // extract domain substring after @ echo "

$welcome

"; // output welcome as heading echo "

Your email domain: $domain

"; // show extracted domain } ?> ``` This ties variables, arrays, string functions, conditionals, loops, and superglobals into a realistic form-processing flow.
keyPoints: PHP is a server-side scripting language embedded in HTML via <?php ?> tags
Variables start with $ and are loosely typed by default
Eight primitive types: boolean, integer, float, string, array, object, resource, null
Double-quoted strings interpolate variables; single-quoted strings do not
Arrays are ordered maps supporting both integer and string keys
Use === for strict comparison to avoid type-juggling surprises

topics.content: ### ## What's This? Control flow and functions are the mechanisms that let your PHP code make decisions, repeat tasks, and organize logic into reusable units. Control flow statements like if, for, and switch determine which code blocks execute based on conditions. Functions package a sequence of statements under a name so you can call them from anywhere without duplicating code. They exist because programs would be unmanageable without conditional logic, loops, and modular organization -- every nontrivial application needs these building blocks. ### ## The Big Picture Control flow and functions form the backbone of every PHP application. Conditionals handle routing logic, input validation, and authorization. Loops process database result sets, arrays, and paginated data. Functions encapsulate everything from validation helpers to database queries. The match expression (PHP 8) and arrow functions provide modern alternatives to older constructs. Mastering these tools is necessary before moving to OOP, frameworks, or any advanced PHP topic. ### ## Core Ideas ### Conditionals: if, elseif, else PHP evaluates a boolean expression and executes the corresponding block. You can chain multiple conditions without limit. ```php if ($score >= 90) { // first condition checked $grade = "A"; // executes only when score >= 90 } elseif ($score >= 80) { // checked only when first is false $grade = "B"; } else { $grade = "F"; // fallback when all conditions fail } ``` ### The match Expression (PHP 8) match is a strict, expression-based alternative to switch. It returns a value and does not require break statements. ```php $statusCode = 404; $message = match ($statusCode) { // match evaluates $statusCode strictly 200 => "OK", // returns "OK" if statusCode === 200 404 => "Not Found", // returns "Not Found" if statusCode === 404 default => "Unknown" // fallback when no arm matches }; // match always returns a value ``` ### Loops: foreach, for, while foreach iterates arrays and objects. for runs a known number of times. while runs until a condition becomes false. ```php foreach ($users as $user) { // loop over each element in $users array echo $user["name"]; // access name key of current user } for ($i = 0; $i < 5; $i++) { // init counter; check condition; increment echo $i; // outputs 0 1 2 3 4 } while ($row = $result->fetch()) { // fetch returns false when no more rows echo $row["title"]; // display title from current row } ``` ### Defining Functions Functions are declared with function, accept typed parameters, and can declare a return type. Default parameter values make arguments optional. ```php function greet(string $name): string { // parameter typed as string, returns string return "Hello, $name!"; // returns the greeting to the caller } function add(int $a, int $b = 0): int { // $b defaults to 0 when not provided return $a + $b; } $result = greet("Alice"); // calls function, $result = "Hello, Alice!" ``` ### Variable Scope Variables declared outside functions are global; variables inside functions are local. The global keyword accesses global scope from within a function. ```php $taxRate = 0.08; // global scope variable function calculateTax(float $price): float { global $taxRate; // imports global $taxRate into function scope return $price * $taxRate; // uses the imported global value } ``` ### Arrow Functions (PHP 7.4+) Arrow functions provide a concise syntax for closures that automatically capture variables from the parent scope by value. ```php $multiplier = 2; $doubled = array_map( // applies callback to each array element fn($n) => $n * $multiplier, // arrow fn automatically captures $multiplier [1, 2, 3] // input array ); // result: [2, 4, 6] ``` ### ## Wiring It Together This script calculates order totals with tax and tiered discounts: ```php 100) { // orders over $100 get 10 percent off return $total * 0.9; // multiply by 0.9 to apply discount } elseif ($total > 50) { // orders over $50 get 5 percent off return $total * 0.95; // multiply by 0.95 for discount } return $total; // no discount for orders $50 or less } function calculateTax(float $subtotal): float { global $taxRate; // pull in global $taxRate variable return $subtotal * $taxRate; // compute tax amount } $items = [29.99, 49.99, 15.00]; // array of item prices $subtotal = 0; // initialize running total foreach ($items as $price) { // iterate every item price $subtotal += $price; // accumulate into subtotal } $afterDiscount = applyDiscount($subtotal); // compute discounted amount $tax = calculateTax($afterDiscount); // compute tax on discounted total $grandTotal = $afterDiscount + $tax; // final amount the customer pays echo "Subtotal: \$$subtotal\n"; // display subtotal before discount echo "After discount: \$$afterDiscount\n"; // show discounted amount echo "Tax: \$$tax\n"; // show computed tax echo "Total: \$$grandTotal\n"; // show final total ?> ``` This example combines conditionals (tiered discount), loops (price iteration), functions with scope (tax/discount), and string interpolation in a practical order-processing scenario.
keyPoints: if/elseif/else evaluates conditions top-down and executes the first true block
match (PHP 8+) is a strict, expression-based switch alternative
foreach loops over arrays; for uses a counter; while checks a condition
Functions declare typed parameters and return types for predictability
Variables are function-scoped by default; use global to import outer scope
Arrow functions (fn) capture outer variables automatically without use keyword
A class is a blueprint; an object is an instance created with new
Visibility controls: public (anywhere), protected (class + subclasses), private (class only)
Inheritance with extends allows child classes to reuse and override parent behavior
Interfaces define contracts; a class can implement multiple interfaces
Traits provide horizontal code reuse to work around single inheritance
Static members belong to the class itself, accessed with ::
Composer is PHP's dependency manager; packages come from Packagist
composer.json defines dependencies; composer.lock pins exact versions
^ prefix means compatible with major version; ~ means patch-level only
PSR-4 autoloading maps namespaces to directories; run dump-autoload after changes
require-dev adds packages only for development/testing
require 'vendor/autoload.php' is the single entry point for all classes
Laravel MVC separates concerns: Model (data), View (presentation), Controller (logic)
Routes defined in web.php or api.php map URLs to controller methods
Blade uses @ directives for control structures and layout inheritance
The service container resolves class dependencies automatically
Resource routes generate all CRUD routes with a single declaration
The request flows: index.php -> kernel -> middleware -> router -> controller -> response
Eloquent is Laravel's Active Record ORM; each model maps to a database table
Migrations version-control your database schema; run php artisan migrate
CRUD: create, save/update, delete, and query with where/get/find
Relationships (hasMany, belongsTo, belongsToMany) handle JOINs automatically
Eager loading with with() prevents the N+1 query problem
Collections provide map, filter, pluck, and other functional methods on result sets
Middleware sits between request and controller; handles cross-cutting concerns
Global middleware runs on all requests; alias middleware applies to specific routes
Authentication guards (session, token, Sanctum) determine how users are verified
Gates are Closure-based authorization; Policies are class-based per model
Throttle middleware limits request rates to prevent abuse
Middleware receives a request, passes it down the pipeline, and gets a response back
PHPUnit is the standard PHP testing framework; Pest offers a more expressive syntax on top
Test methods use assertions like assertEquals, assertTrue, and assertDatabaseHas
Data providers run the same test with multiple input sets
Mocks replace real dependencies to verify interactions without side effects
Laravel HTTP tests simulate requests in-memory with helpers like actingAs and postJson
RefreshDatabase trait resets the database between tests for isolation
Plugins extend functionality; themes control presentation; never edit core files
Actions run code at specific points; filters modify data before output
Shortcodes are macros that expand to dynamic content in post editor
The Loop iterates through posts using have_posts() and the_post()
WP_Query creates custom database queries outside the main Loop
Always enqueue scripts and styles with wp_enqueue_script/wp_enqueue_style

topics.content: ### ## What's This? Deployment and tooling in PHP covers the process of taking your application from a development environment to a production server where real users can access it. This includes environment configuration, CI/CD pipelines, server provisioning, caching, queue management, and monitoring. Deployment exists because running code on your local machine is fundamentally different from running it on a production server -- differences in PHP versions, extensions, database credentials, and performance requirements must be handled systematically to prevent downtime and security issues. ### ## The Big Picture PHP deployment has evolved from FTP-uploading files to sophisticated CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Laravel Forge. Modern tooling includes Docker for consistent environments, Envoyer for zero-downtime deployments, and services like Laravel Vapor for serverless PHP. Performance optimization involves OPcache, config caching, queue workers, and CDN integration. A proper deployment workflow includes automated testing, environment separation (development/staging/production), secret management, and monitoring with tools like Flare or Sentry. ### ## Core Ideas ### Environment Configuration Environment variables separate configuration from code. Laravel uses a .env file for local development and sets real environment variables on the server. Never commit secrets to version control. ```php // .env file (never committed to Git) APP_ENV=production // current environment name APP_DEBUG=false // disable debug mode in production DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 // database host address DB_DATABASE=blog // database name DB_USERNAME=deploy_user // database user DB_PASSWORD=secret // database password (keep secret) // Access in code $dbHost = env('DB_HOST', 'localhost'); // get env var with fallback default $isProduction = env('APP_ENV') === 'production'; // boolean check for environment ``` ### Deployment Pipeline (CI/CD) A CI/CD pipeline automatically runs tests, builds assets, and deploys your application. GitHub Actions is a common choice for PHP projects. ```yaml # .github/workflows/deploy.yml name: Deploy on: push: branches: [main] // trigger on pushes to main branch jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 // checkout repository code - uses: shivammathur/setup-php@v2 // install PHP with extensions with: php-version: '8.2' - run: composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader // install prod deps - run: php artisan config:cache // cache config for performance - run: php artisan route:cache // cache routes for performance - run: php artisan migrate --force // run database migrations (forced) ``` ### Laravel Optimization Commands Laravel provides Artisan commands to cache configurations, routes, and views. These dramatically improve performance by reducing file parsing on each request. ```bash # Run these on each deployment before putting the site live php artisan config:cache # merge all config files into one cached file php artisan route:cache # serialize route registrations for fast loading php artisan view:cache # pre-compile all Blade templates to plain PHP php artisan event:cache # cache event/listener registrations php artisan optimize # run all of the above at once php artisan queue:restart # restart queue workers to pick up code changes ``` ### OPcache OPcache stores compiled PHP scripts in shared memory, eliminating the need to parse and compile on every request. Enable and configure it in php.ini. ```ini ; php.ini OPcache configuration for production opcache.enable=1 ; enable OPcache globally opcache.memory_consumption=128 ; allocate 128MB for cached compiled scripts opcache.max_accelerated_files=10000 ; maximum number of cached PHP files opcache.validate_timestamps=0 ; disable timestamp checks in production (faster) ``` ### Queues and Workers PHP queues handle time-consuming tasks (email, image processing) asynchronously. Laravel's queue system supports Redis, database, and SQS drivers. Workers process jobs in the background. ```php // Dispatching a job to the queue use App\Jobs\SendWelcomeEmail; SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch($user); // push job onto the default queue SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch($user)->onQueue('emails'); // push to specific queue // Start queue worker (supervisor keeps it running) // php artisan queue:work --queue=emails,default --sleep=3 --tries=3 // Supervisor configuration (/etc/supervisor/conf.d/laravel-worker.conf) [program:laravel-worker] process_name=%(program_name)s_%(process_num)02d command=php /var/www/artisan queue:work --sleep=3 --tries=3 --max-time=3600 autostart=true ; start worker when supervisor starts autorestart=true ; restart worker if it crashes numprocs=4 ; run 4 worker processes in parallel ``` ### Server Provisioning (Laravel Forge) Laravel Forge automates server provisioning on DigitalOcean, AWS, Linode, and others. It installs Nginx, PHP, MySQL, Redis, and configures queue workers, cron jobs, and SSL certificates. ```bash # Forge handles these tasks automatically: # - Creates a server with Nginx, PHP 8.x, MySQL/PostgreSQL, Redis # - Configures Nginx sites with SSL via Let's Encrypt # - Sets up queue workers with Supervisor # - Configures cron jobs for scheduled tasks (php artisan schedule:run) # - Manages deployment scripts (git pull, composer install, migrations) # - Monitors server health and sends alerts # # Example deployment script configured in Forge: # cd /home/forge/example.com # git pull origin main # composer install --no-dev --no-interaction --optimize-autoloader # if [ -f artisan ]; then # php artisan migrate --force # php artisan config:cache # php artisan route:cache # php artisan view:cache # php artisan queue:restart # fi ``` ### ## Wiring It Together A complete GitHub Actions deployment workflow for a Laravel application: ```yaml # .github/workflows/deploy.yml name: Deploy Laravel Application on: push: branches: [main] jobs: test-and-deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Checkout code uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Setup PHP uses: shivammathur/setup-php@v2 with: php-version: '8.2' extensions: mbstring, pdo_mysql, redis, imagick - name: Install dependencies run: composer install --no-progress --prefer-dist --optimize-autoloader - name: Run tests run: php artisan test // run PHPUnit test suite env: DB_CONNECTION: sqlite // use SQLite for CI testing DB_DATABASE: :memory: - name: Deploy to production if: success() // only deploy if tests pass run: | # Using Forge CLI or SSH deploy # forge deploy your-site-id # Or manually via SSH: ssh deploy@example.com " cd /var/www/app && git pull origin main && composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader && php artisan migrate --force && php artisan config:cache && php artisan route:cache && php artisan view:cache && php artisan queue:restart " ``` ```php // config/deploy.php -- deploy configuration checklist return [ 'environments' => [ 'local' => [ 'debug' => true, 'opcache' => false, ], 'staging' => [ 'debug' => true, 'opcache' => true, ], 'production' => [ 'debug' => false, // never show errors in production 'opcache' => true, // always enable OPcache 'config_cache' => true, // cache config on deploy 'queue_driver' => 'redis', // use Redis for production queues ], ], ]; ``` This ties together environment configuration (env vars), CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions), Laravel optimization (config/route/view cache), database migrations, and queue management into a production-ready deployment workflow.
keyPoints: .env files store environment-specific configuration; never commit secrets to Git
CI/CD pipelines automatically test and deploy code on push to main branch
Laravel optimization: cache config, routes, views, and events for faster response times
OPcache stores compiled PHP in memory; disable timestamp validation in production
Queue workers process background jobs asynchronously; Supervisor keeps them running
Laravel Forge automates server provisioning, Nginx setup, SSL, and deployment scripting
